newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower on hydro, weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower on hydro, weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Wednesday on mild weather in most of the western U.S. and expected deluge of cheap hydroelectric supplies from pending spring runoffs in the Northwest.
"Fundamentals are still pretty bearish," said one Houston futures trader.
The power complex fell in line with sharply lower cash and over-the-counter prices, market sources said.

Firm, peak power prices for day-ahead delivery at Palo Verde (PV) were quoted at $18.50-19.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), down one to two dollars from Tuesday, while those at California-Oregon Border (COB) were assessed at $13.50-14.50 down from Tuesday's $14.75-15.75.

Prices in the Southwest did not drop as much as the Northwest market due to continued high temperatures which have triggered some air conditioning demand as well as continued scattered power plant outages.

The 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was expected to restart tomorrow and reach full output this weekend. The unit has been off line since November 30 for refueling and maintenance.
The 750 MW coal-fired Four Corners unit 5 in New Mexico 750 MW was planned to resume operating Saturday after being shut more than a week ago for repairs.
Moreover, a 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired facility in Wyoming was expected to shut later today for extended maintenance through mid-April.
April COB futures settled at $10.16, down 69 cents after traded between $10.00 and $10.70. May COB finished down 35 cents at $9.50. Other COB months ended flat to 10 cents lower.
April PV settled down 53 cents at $14.35, near the day's low of $14.30. May PV finished down 40 cents at $14.35. Outer PV months ended flat to 30 cents lower.
Most market sources said power futures would likely head lower tomorrow, but some players are ready to build long positions if the complex drops any further.
"A lot of people are ready to go long in anticipation of summer demand," said the Houston trader.
"They look like pretty good buy levels," said an East Coast paper broker.

In the Northwest, low pressure systems would continue to dump rain along the coast over the next several days. Temperatures would run 14 degrees above normal in the extreme southeast to about four degrees above normal in the northwest.
In the Southwest, readings were called to average about 14 degrees above normal in the northeast as well as in the southern deserts, to about five degrees above normal in the extreme northwest.
NYMEX estimated 184 COB and 304 PV contracts were sold, down from 171 COB and 275 PV lots Tuesday.
